relevance_note: Case series of four children with TNFAIP3 variants: "We describe four unrelated patients evaluated at a single tertiary center, each carrying a distinct TNFAIP3 mutation".
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values and spans typed from my reading, and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown (no table was transcribed by script). Labels: the paper's own letters A-D (Table 1 'Patient' column and case text). Scope: relatives included when affected (oral ulcers, HA20, lupus, rheumatic fever etc.) or tested (both parents of D tested negative). Left out: A's unaffected brother, A's sister with neurodevelopmental delay, B's mother and second brother (unaffected, untested), C's two unaffected sisters, D's older brother with anxiety and epilepsy (paper calls the family history otherwise negative; not tested); also the mother and grandmother of the ref (26) patient (only a Behcet's diagnosis given) and the p.Q379* breast marginal zone lymphoma patients of ref (25) (group mention, tumour context). Four previously published individuals from the Discussion were included (refs (15, 16), (2, 12, 22), (24), (26)) because each has a variant plus sex or features; the ref (24) p.Trp168* HA20+DLBCL patient may be the same person as B's father ('as found in the father of patient B (24)') - wording ambiguous, kept separate, and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null. Father of B: variant row uses B's printed variant because the paper says he 'has HA20 of the same genetic variant'; his zygosity left not reported. Paternal grandfather of B 'also had HA20' but no TNFAIP3 variant is tied to him, so no variant row. Variant type: only A's p.Pro247Leu is named missense; the paper's 'Three out of four patients had non-sense mutations' does not name them, so B, C, D variant type left not reported (v5). Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' taken from Discussion sentences naming each exact variant (p.Trp168*, p.Arg271*, p.Q379*), also applied to literature patients and B's father carrying that exact variant. is_proband left null for A-D (paper does not call them probands; not a single-patient case report). D's age at HA20 diagnosis not stated as such (presentation at 13 years then exome testing), left not reported; D's CRP of 60.9 mg/L is given without being called elevated, so not recorded as a feature and the CRP/ESR checklist item is not reported. A's 'negative for uveitis and retinal vasculitis' recorded as excluded features but does not exclude the broader checklist items 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' or 'vasculitis'. D-27: B's 'normal chest x-ray (CXR) and electrocardiogram' and D's normal sinus/pulmonary CT recorded only as excluded abnormal investigations, nothing more specific; B's later CXR showed pleural effusions (different time point, not treated as a contradiction). A's 'poor weight gain' mapped to the growth failure checklist item (judgement). Father of B's 'aphthous ulcers' mapped to oral ulcers and 'significant cutaneous findings' to skin lesions (judgement). Great-grandmother's 'joint issues' not mapped to arthritis or arthralgia (too vague). Fever without 'recurrent' (B, ref (26)) not mapped to recurrent fever. First author: header lists 'Jayaraman Sahana'; author contributions use initials 'SJ', so surname taken as Jayaraman. No contradictions found within the paper.
